item.title: The Best Cards From Japan's New Yu-Gi-Oh! Core Booster: Immortal Phoenix
item.description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!|competitive

The Best Cards From Japan's New Yu-Gi-Oh! Core Booster: Immortal Phoenix

Winged Dragon of Ra fans rejoice, you're finally able to embrace your inner Yami Marik.

By Samuel Frew

|

Published Nov 16, 2026

|

35 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Kia ora koutou! Immortal Phoenix has released in Japan, bringing 80 new cards to the Yu-Gi-Oh! Official Card Game, including four new large themes, several support waves, further support for themes introduced in Beyond the Brave, and numerous free agents. There's a lot to be interested in, and I'll be covering the best cards in this article.

The Best Cards From Immortal Phoenix

Return of the Sun God

The flagship theme of Immortal Phoenix is the Sun God theme based on Yami Marik's monsters from Yu-Gi-Oh! This theme is based around leveraging the new Spell Card The Immortal Sun God, both to summon your ace monster and to gain advantage through the effects of your other Sun God monsters.

A key point of difference between the Sun God theme and the other large themes in Immortal Phoenix is that Sun Gods require older cards to function, specifically The Winged Dragon of Ra and The True Sun God (the latter of which and Sun God Unification are supported by these new cards).

The Immortal Sun God

Special Summon 1 "The Winged Dragon of Ra" monster from your GY or banishment, ignoring its Summoning conditions, then if you Special Summoned "The Winged Dragon of Ra" by this effect, you can send it to the GY, and if you do, Special Summon 1 "The Winged Dragon of Ra" monster from your Extra Deck. During the End Phase, send the monsters Special Summoned by this effect to the GY. During your Main Phase, if this card is in your GY: You can discard 1 "Sun God" card; add this card to your hand. You can only use each effect of "The Immortal Sun God" once per turn.

The Immortal Sun God can revive a The Winged Dragon of Ra monster for a single turn, but if you revived The Winged Dragon of Ra itself, you'll be able to send it back to the graveyard and Special Summon The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness from your Extra Deck. The Sun God Leading Down into Darkness can send Ra from anywhere to the graveyard to facilitate.

Getting out such a powerful monster for free is awesome, but there are a few caveats. Firstly, the revived monster is sent to the graveyard at the end of the turn, and this effect is applied before the monster is summoned, so The Winged Dragon of Ra - Immortal Phoenix and The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness will still be sent to the graveyard despite being unaffected by other cards' effects. Secondly, you won't be able to revive either The Winged Dragon of Ra - Immortal Phoenix or The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness unless they were properly summoned first, and since The Immortal Sun God doesn't properly Special Summon Sun God of Darkness, you'll have to play multiple copies of that monster if you want to summon it multiple times.

The other effect of The Immortal Sun God allows you to discard another Sun God card to add it from your graveyard to your hand. This gives you fuel for the discard effects of The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness or Helpoemer, Chanter of the Sun God, which is more important than it seems because of the shared effect of the Sun God monsters!

Helpoemer, Chanter of the Sun God

You can discard 1 other card; Special Summon this card from your hand. If this card is Special Summoned: You can add 1 "Sun God" card from your Deck to your hand, except "Helpoemer, Chanter of the Sun God", then if your opponent's LP are at least 2000 higher than yours, you can discard 1 random card from their hand. During the End Phase, if "The Immortal Sun God" was sent to your GY this turn: You can add this card from your GY to your hand. You can only use each effect of "Helpoemer, Chanter of the Sun God" once per turn.

Helpoemer, Chanter of the Sun God is the perfect example: all the Main Deck Sun God monsters have the effect to add themselves back to your hand during the End Phase if The Immortal Sun God was sent to your graveyard that turn, be it from your hand, or Deck, destroyed by your opponent, or sent there because you activated it. As there are four Sun God monsters and you'll want to be sending them to the graveyard for the effects of The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness, this kind of card advantage is sorely welcome.

Helpoemer, Chanter of the Sun God is the main starter card for Sun Gods. Its autocorrection effect to discard a card to Special Summon itself and search a Sun God card can fix suboptimal hands or accelerate your strategy by sending cards like The Winged Dragon of Ra, The Winged Dragon of Ra - Immortal Phoenix, The Immortal Sun God, Makyura, Destructor of the Sun God or Sun God Domination to your graveyard, then search the necessary card to leverage them. As a bonus, it takes out a random card from your opponent's hand if they have at least 2000 more LP than you, which will often be the case if you summon this card after using The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness.

Generally, you'll want to search The Sun God Leading Down into Darkness, using that to send The Winged Dragon of Ra to the graveyard, and then search Makyrua, Destructor of the Sun God if you didn't already trigger that monster, allowing Makyura to grab another Sun God Spell or Trap.

The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness

"The Winged Dragon of Ra" + 3 "Sun God" monsters

Unaffected by other cards' effects. Once per turn, during the Main Phase (Quick Effect): You can discard any number of "Sun God" cards, then choose that number of your opponent's used Main Monster Zones; your opponent must send monsters in those zones to the GY. When an attack is declared involving this card: You can pay LP so that you only have 1 left; this card gains ATK/DEF equal to the LP paid and the total ATK of "Sun God" monsters in your GY.

It's about time to get to the main Sun God monster, The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness. This DIVINE Divine-Beast Fusion ordinarily requires the original Ra and three Sun God monsters, but as Sun Gods don't have an in-theme Fusion Spell you'll most often be Special Summoning it with The Immortal Sun God.

All of the effects of The Winged Dragon of Ra, Sun God of Darkness are incredible: it's unaffected by other card effects, it has a Quick Effect that forces your opponent to send their monsters to the graveyard and the cost allows you to potentially trigger the effects of your Sun God monsters to add themselves back to your hand at the end of the turn, and it can skyrocket to insane ATK levels by paying all but 1 of your LP. It can't be understated how well the cost works with the rest of the theme and this card's effects.

The biggest downside to Sun God of Darkness is that it'll be sent to the graveyard at the end of the turn and leave you with 1 LP, but you can alleviate some of the downsides with Sun God Domination, sacrificing Sun God of Darkness after it attacks to gain LP equal to its ATK, and The Sun God Leading Down into Darkness, which restores 1000 LP each time you destroy a monster in battle.

Amazoness Dramatically Rescue Harpies

Amazoness and Harpies have combined in a new theme centered around cards that mention Harpie Lady, representing Mai Valentine's deck from Battle City, and it's a doozy. The new Amazoness and Harpie cards bolster Amazoness, Harpies, and work extremely well together, making for an effective offensive deck that also forces your opponent to fight your battle.

Amazoness Spellcaster - Forbidden Spell Dance

If this card is Normal or Special Summoned: You can add 1 "Amazoness" monster from your Deck to your hand, except a Level 3 monster. During your Main Phase: You can Fusion Summon 1 EARTH or WIND Fusion Monster from your Extra Deck, using monsters from your hand or field. During damage calculation, if your "Amazoness" monster battles an opponent's monster: You can banish this card from your GY; switch the battling monsters' ATK until the end of this turn. You can only use each effect of "Amazoness Spellcaster - Forbidden Spell Dance" once per turn.

Amazoness Spellcaster - Forbidden Spell Dance gets things started by searching a non-Level 3 Amazoness when it's summoned, and if you search Amazoness Fighter - Instant Kill Dance, that monster can Special Summon itself from your hand and Set a Spell or Trap from your deck that mentions Harpie Lady. Amazoness Spellcaster - Forbidden Spell Dance then progresses things further by Fusion Summoning either an EARTH (Amazoness) or WIND (Harpie) Fusion Monster, allowing combos to snowball from there. 

Despite her name, Amazoness Spellcaster - Forbidden Spell Dance is a Warrior monster, so you can search it with both Reinforcement of the Army or the pre-existing Amazoness Call (which can itself be searched by Amazoness War Chief). Conversely, the new Elegant Tri-Mirror fills the same role for Harpies, essentially giving you doubled consistency for the strategy. As a final bonus, you can banish Amazoness Spellcaster - Forbidden Spell Dance from your graveyard to recreate the original Amazoness Spellcaster, switching the ATK of your Amazoness monster with its opponent to ensure it comes out on top.

Amazoness Swordsmaster

2 "Amazoness" monsters

When your "Amazoness" monster destroys an opponent's monster by battle: You can draw 1 card. You can only use each of the following effects of "Amazoness Swordmaster" once per turn. If this card is Fusion Summoned: You can Special Summon 1 Level 4 or lower "Amazoness" monster from your Deck. (Quick Effect): You can Tribute 1 monster, then target 1 Effect Monster on the field; it loses 500 ATK, also negate its effects.

The two Fusion Monsters for the Amazoness Harpie strategy in Immortal Phoenix are absolutely incredible. Amazoness Swordsmaster is the first Amazoness Fusion Monster to simply require two Amazoness monsters as material and offers some fantastic effects for such ease of summoning (remembering that between the Darkwing Blast support and Immortal Phoenix support there are tons of ways to get to Fusion Summoning effects to access). 

Once Fusion Summoned, Amazoness Swordmaster Special Summons a Level 4 or lower Amazoness monster from your deck, providing perfect fuel for its Quick Effect to sacrifice a monster to negate the effects of an Effect Monster and reduce its ATK by 500, although you can sacrifice Amazoness Swordmaster itself in a pinch. You can also draw a card each time your Amazoness monster destroys a monster in battle, contributing to the strategy's resource climb.

Triangle Ecstasy Harpie Lady Sisters

3 "Harpie Lady" monsters

Must first be Fusion Summoned. This card's name becomes "Harpie Lady" while on the field or in the GY. Gains 500 ATK for each "Harpie Lady" in your GY, also your opponent cannot target this card with non-WIND monster effects. Once per turn (Quick Effect): You can destroy all Spells/Traps your opponent controls.

Harpies finally have a Fusion Monster, Triangle Ecstasy Harpie Lady Sisters, which can be fused from three Harpie Lady monsters, not just the original Harpie Lady, allowing you to use monsters like the new Harpie Lady - Alluring Dance and Harpie Lady - Elegant Egotist (the latter from Original Artwork Collection) while they're in your hand and thus not treated as Harpie Lady. Speaking of Harpie Lady - Elegant Egotist, she's easily the most effective way of amassing the necessary materials to Fusion Summon this monster (another example of the themes in this set not quite being standalone).

Triangle Ecstasy Harpie Lady Sisters starts at 3000 ATK but gains 500 for each Harpie Lady in your graveyard; with the minimum of three needed to Fusion Summon it, it will have 4500 ATK. Triangle Ecstasy Harpie Lady Sisters also packs immunity to targeting effects from non-WIND monsters and a built-in Harpie's Feather Duster as a Quick Effect.

Eyelluring Mirror Wall

Gains these effects while you control an "Amazoness" monster or "Harpie Lady".

  • Face-up monsters your opponent controls are changed to Attack Position and must attack if able.
  • Once per battle, when an opponent's monster declares an attack: You can halve its ATK.

Once per turn, during the Standby Phase: You can Set 1 Spell/Trap from your GY or banishment that mentions "Harpie Lady", except "Eyelluring Mirror Wall".

For a Continuous Trap themed around battle, Eyelluring Mirror Wall is surprisingly effective! While you have an Amazoness monster or Harpie Lady out, your opponent's monsters will be forced to attack yours with half their ATK, making them easy prey, particularly as the ATK reduction is permanent. 

However, even better is Eyelluring Mirror Wall's effect to Set a Spell or Trap from your graveyard or banishment that mentions Harpie Lady, allowing you to recur cards like the excellent new Amazoness Dramatic Rescue, Elegant Tri-Mirror, Elegant Egotist and Hysteric Party. Amazoness Dramatic Rescue is a particularly excellent option to continue recovering given its own effect to banish itself from your graveyard and recover a Harpie or Amazoness monster. In combination with Eyelluring Mirror Wall, it's a surprisingly grindy duo!

Winter Raven, White Forest

The Winter Raven theme is loosely based on past Sinful Spoils themes, and as such plays together nicely with them while advancing its own game plan of manipulating cards in the Spell & Trap Zones and Fusion Summoning using your Synchro Monsters.

Mart, Knight of the Winter Raven

You can send 1 other card from your hand or field to the GY; place this card face-up in its owner's Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell, and if you do, Special Summon up to 2 "Winter Raven" monsters with different names from each other from your Deck, except "Mart, Knight of the Winter Raven". When a monster declares an attack and this card is a Continuous Spell: You can target 1 "Winter Raven" Monster Card in your Spell & Trap Zone; Special Summon it. You can only use each effect of "Mart, Knight of the Winter Raven" once per turn.

Mart, Knight of the Winter Raven is a one-card starter that places himself in your Spell & Trap Zone by sending another card to the graveyard and then Special Summons two different Winter Raven monsters from your deck. Ideally you'll be after Purifire of the Winter Raven's Forest and Anu, Knight of the Winter Raven, both to get the necessary materials for a Winter Raven Synchro Monster and to utterly expand your available moves.

With Purifire, you can also search a Winter Raven Spell/Trap or a Sinful Spoils card like WANTED: Seeker of Sinful Spoils, while the Illusion Winter Ravens can be fused with Elzette, Azamina of the White Forest into Azamina Mu Rcielago to search another Sinful Spoils card. Sinful Spoils of the White Forest is another that deserves mention, as it can summon the Illusion Winter Ravens and the Spellcaster Sinful Spoils of the Winter Raven's Forest, or be a Fusion Spell to Fusion Summon Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest.

In all honesty, this is barely scratching the surface of the stuff you can do with this theme.

Sinful Spoils of the Winter Raven's Forest

You can Special Summon this card (from your hand) by placing 1 Level 1 FIRE Monster Card from your face-up field or GY on the bottom of the Deck. You can only Special Summon "Sinful Spoils of the Winter Raven's Forest" once per turn this way. When your opponent activates a card or effect (Quick Effect): You can return this card from the field to the hand, then target 1 face-up monster on the field or in either GY; place it face-up in its owner's Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell. You can only use this effect of "Sinful Spoils of the Winter Raven's Forest" once per turn.

Sinful Spoils of the Winter Raven's Forest is less part of the Winter Raven combo and more a feature. She doesn't move the strategy to get to Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest along, she shows up by putting a Level 1 FIRE Monster Card like Purifire (or yes, Snake-Eyes Poplar) on the bottom of your deck and as soon as your opponent sneezes in her presence, she returns herself to your hand and places a monster from either side of the field or graveyard into the Spell & Trap Zone. The flexibility of this effect is great, as you can remove a troublesome card, or fuel your own Spell & Trap Zone in response to a handtrap and give the eventual Diabellze even more potency.

Zaltys, Knight of the Winter Raven

1 Illusion Tuner + 1+ non-Tuners

If this card is Special Summoned: You can target up to 2 Spells/Traps on the field; return them to the hand. If this card is sent to the GY: You can activate this effect based on where it was sent from;

  • Field: Set 1 "Winter Raven" Trap from your Deck.
  • Extra Deck: Add 1 "Winter Raven" card from your GY to your hand.

You can only use each effect of "Zaltys, Knight of the Winter Raven" once per turn.

Both Winter Raven Synchro Monsters are pretty excellent, but Zaltys, Knight of the Winter Raven has a ton of potential in what he can do. When he's Special Summoned, he can return up to two Spell and Trap Cards on the field to the hand, variably clearing out your opponent's backrow or adjusting your own. As all the Main Deck Winter Raven monsters have their own effects to summon themselves and many have effects to summon other cards, this effect, in addition to Zaltys' effect when sent from the Extra Deck to the graveyard, allows you to put them in the position to use them that turn as well. His effect when sent to the graveyard from your field is also vital to Fusion Summon Diabellze, Heiress of the White Forest in-theme, as he can Set one of the Winter Raven Traps from your deck.

Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest

1 Fusion or Synchro Monster + 1 Spellcaster or Illusion monster

If this card is Special Summoned: You can place any number of monsters you control face-up in their owners' Spell & Trap Zones as Continuous Spells, then you can return cards on the field to the hand up to the number of Spells/Traps you control. You can only use this effect of "Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest" once per turn. Gains 700 ATK/DEF for each Spell/Trap on the field. This face-up Fusion Summoned card cannot be used as Fusion Material.

Diabellze, Heiress of the Winter Raven's Forest packs a spectacular removal effect when it's Special Summoned, placing any number of monsters you control in the Spell & Trap Zone and then returning cards to the hand equal to the number of Spells and Traps you control, for a maximum of six if you have Deep Forest of the Winter Raven on the field. She also gains 700 ATK and DEF for each Spell or Trap on the field, and can't be used as material herself, preventing your opponent from using Super Polymerization shenanigans on her.

Although, Super Polymerization actually works quite well to Fusion Summon Diabellze herself! Given that her materials are reasonably flexible, your opponent might provide the necessary Fusion or Synchro Monster to Fusion Summon her. The Winter Raven cards that can natively Fusion Summon Diabellze are all Traps, though those fortunately can variably use monsters in your Extra Deck, allowing you to leverage the effects of the Winter Raven Synchro Monsters when sent from the Extra Deck to the graveyard, particularly Aitvaras, Knight of the Winter Raven to put a Winter Raven monster on the field for Diabellze to stick in the Spell & Trap Zone.

Salamangreats Rise Again

Salamangreats got some excellent consistency options that also add a new anti-FIRE strategy to the theme, and quite handily minimize the number of cards you need to add to their Extra Deck despite debuting a new Link Monster.

Salamangreat Markhor

If this card is Normal or Special Summoned: You can add 1 "Salamangreat" Spell/Trap from your Deck or GY to your hand. If this card is sent to the GY as material for a Link-3 or higher FIRE Link Monster: You can Special Summon 1 FIRE Cyberse monster from your Deck. You can only use each effect of "Salamangreat Markhor" once per turn, also you cannot Special Summon the turn you activate either of this card's effects, except FIRE monsters.

Salamangreat Markhor is a fantastic bit of consistency and extension in a single card. If it's Normal or Special Summoned, you can search a Salamangreat Spell or Trap or you can get it back from the graveyard. Considering the hoops you had to jump through previously to get specific Salamangreat Spells and Traps, Markhor's effect would be tremendously welcome even if it only added from the deck, but it can recover cards as well! You can also Special Summon a FIRE Cyberse monster from your deck if you use Markhor as material for a LINK-3 or higher FIRE Link Monster, allowing for further extension.

Salamangreat Shrine

(This card is always treated as "Salamangreat Sanctuary".)

"Salamangreat" monsters you control are unaffected by your opponent's activated FIRE monsters' effects. You can only use each of the following effects of "Salamangreat Shrine" once per turn. If you Link Summon a "Salamangreat" Link Monster, you can use 1 "Salamangreat" Link Monster you control with its same name as the entire material. During your Main Phase: You can shuffle any number of "Salamangreat" cards from your hand into the Deck, then draw the same number of cards.

Salamangreat Shrine is an anime-imported twist on Salamangreat Sanctuary. Despite being treated as Salamangreat Sanctuary, it's not meant to replace it but compliment it. Both cards have the effect to Reincarnation Link Summon, but Shrine has additional effects that make it worthy to keep around. First, it gives you the chance to shuffle unwanted Salamangreat cards back into your deck and draw the same number of cards, and most importantly, it protects your Salamangreats from the activated effects of your opponent's FIRE monsters.

King of Beasts, Risen from the Valley of Flames

3 FIRE Effect Monsters

(This card is always treated as "Salamangreat Heatleo".)

Face-up monsters on the field become FIRE. During the Main Phase, if this card was Link Summoned using "Salamangreat Heatleo" (Quick Effect): You can target 1 card your opponent controls; shuffle it into the Deck, then you can make the ATK of 1 FIRE monster your opponent controls become the ATK of 1 monster in your GY. You can only use this effect of "King of Beasts, Risen from the Valley of Flames" once per turn.

On top of blunting decks like Fire Kings with Salamangreat Shrine, you can also make all your opponent's monsters into FIRE monsters with the effect of the new King of Beasts, Risen from the Valley of Flames. This monster is always treated as Salamangreat Heatleo, allowing it to slot into your existing Salamangreat Extra Deck with no issues if you already ran it, and its reincarnated Quick Effect allows you to shuffle 1 card your opponent controls into the deck and match the ATK of a FIRE monster your opponent controls with the ATK of a monster in your graveyard. 

Medius Lore

There are two themes from the Medius lore getting support in Immortal Phoenix: Ars Magna, and Power Patron. 

Omega Vidolium the Power Patron of Heaven's End

Pendulum Effect: If a monster(s) is Special Summoned from the Extra Deck (except during the Damage Step): You can return this card to the Extra Deck, then you can Fusion Summon 1 Fusion Monster from your Extra Deck, using monsters from either field, including a "Power Patron" monster you control.

Monster Effect: 3 monsters Special Summoned from the Extra Deck with 3000 or more ATK

Must first be Fusion Summoned. Unaffected by card effects, except "Power Patron" cards'. When your opponent activates a monster effect while they control 2 or more monsters with the same Type as that monster (Quick Effect): You can banish (face-down) the top 3 cards of your Deck; negate the activation, and if you do, banish that monster face-down. Once per turn, during your Standby Phase: Place this card in your Pendulum Zone.

Don't think that Omega Vidolium the Power Patron of Heaven's End is difficult to summon just because he's a Fusion-Pendulum Monster! Power Patron Portal Plugging -Sword of Mutual Destruction- can place him from your Extra Deck into your Pendulum Zone and then grab another Power Patron Pendulum from your deck, completing your Pendulum Scales and more consistently getting Jupredo the Shademachine Power Patron. Then, if either player Special Summons a monster from the Extra Deck, Omega Vidolium can return himself to the Extra Deck to Fusion Summon using monsters from either field, as long as you use at least one Power Patron you control. This flexibility means you can Fusion Summon Omega Vidolium using monsters from your own field or spring it on an opponent if you can anticipate their field.

Once Omega Vidolium is out, it boats 4000 ATK and DEF and is unaffected by non-Power Patron card effects. In addition, it's crippling against decks that rely on the same Type of monster, as it can negate the effect of your opponent's monster and banish that monster face-down if your opponent controlled two more monsters with the same Type, and as long as your opponent keeps putting enough monsters on the field, there's no limit to the number of times Omega Vidolium can do this. Its mandatory effect to place it in your Pendulum Zone is less of a downside given it can just be re-fused easily enough, potentially using more of your opponent's monsters as material.

Ars Magna Academic Arcane Apparition Acropolis

(This card is always treated as an "Artmage" card.)

Your activated "Medius" monsters' effects cannot be negated. If you have a "Power Patron" monster in your GY: You can banish 1 Fusion, Synchro, or Xyz Monster from your GY, and declare 1 "Ars Magna" Link Monster Card name that has not been declared for "Ars Magna Academic Arcane Apparition Acropolis" this turn; Special Summon that monster from your Extra Deck, but it cannot be used as Link Material.

Ars Magna Academic Arcane Apparition Acropolis (which I am hereby declaring "Ars Magna" for the rest of this paragraph) fits into an interesting spot in the Ars Magna theme. It prevents your activated Medius monster effects from being negated, making Theorealized Medius even better, and as Theorealized Medius is also a Power Patron monster, he fulfils the other effect of Ars Magna to permit you to banish a Fusion, Synchro or Xyz Monster from your graveyard and Special Summon an Ars Magna Link Monster from your Extra Deck. 

These Link Monsters provide different advantages to Mediclius the Extraordinary Power Patron compared to the Main Deck Ars Magna monsters, especially if you have Ars Magna "Citrinitas" out to turn their effects into Quick Effects. Ars Magna Elfnote can bounce a monster back to your opponent's hand and increase the ATK of linked monsters further, Ars Magna DoomZ can destroy a card you control to disrupt the graveyard, and Ars Magna Artmage can provide targeting protection for your linked monsters.

Dark Time Wizard

Just as Light and Darkness Ritual received two legacy support cards in Beyond the Brave, Dark Time Wizard got two follow-up cards in Immortal Phoenix, and they're both awesome for the deck.

Invincible Rocket Warrior

Cannot be destroyed by card effects. You can only use each of the following effects of "Invincible Rocket Warrior" once per turn. You can send 1 Spell/Trap that mentions "Dark Time Wizard" from your Deck to the GY; Special Summon this card from your hand, then you can make 1 monster your opponent controls lose 1500 ATK, also you cannot Special Summon from the Extra Deck for the rest of this turn, except Fusion Monsters. When this card declares an attack: You can add 1 Level 4 Warrior monster from your Deck to your hand.

Invincible Rocket Warrior has two important purposes. Firstly, it's a Mathmech Circular for Dark Time Wizard, sending one of their Spells or Traps from the deck to the graveyard to Special Summon itself and reduce the ATK of one of your opponent's monsters (if they have any) by a large 1500. Sending Foolish Graverobber to the graveyard lets you retrieve a Spell or Trap that mentions Dark Time Wizard, and if you already have Foolish Graverobber in your graveyard or plan to summon The Legendary Insect Queen, you can instead send the Spell or Trap you need to add to your hand.

Invincible Rocket Warrior's second effect to search a Level 4 Warrior might not seem like much initially, but it's meant to tie Gearfried the Steel Knight and Gilford the Lightning, the Warrior of Thunderbolts into the Dark Time Wizard deck. Invincible Rocket Warrior can search Gearfried the Steel Knight, and if one of your monsters was destroyed that turn (be it in battle or by Dark Time Wizard earlier) Gearfried the Steel Knight can Special Summon himself from your hand and power himself up by 800 ATK via equipping a monster from your graveyard. Equip the Level 4 LIGHT Warrior Invincible Rocket Warrior, and Gearfried the Steel Knight can send it to the graveyard to search the Level 8 LIGHT Warrior Gilford the Lightning, the Warrior of Thunderbolts.
As a final bonus, Invincible Rocket Warrior can't be destroyed by card effects, so Dark Time Wizard won't wipe it out if you call the coin toss incorrectly.

The Legendary Insect Queen

2 monsters that mention "Dark Time Wizard", and/or Level 1 EARTH Tokens

Must be either Fusion Summoned, or Special Summoned (from your Extra Deck) by Tributing the above monsters. You can only Special Summon "The Legendary Insect Queen" once per turn this way, no matter which method you use. If this card is Special Summoned: You can add up to 2 cards that mention "Dark Time Wizard" from your GY and/or banishment to your hand. Your opponent cannot target other cards you control that mention "Dark Time Wizard" with card effects.

The Legendary Insect Queen is a second Fusion Monster for Dark Time Wizard that provides targeting protection for your other Dark Time Wizard cards and allows you to make a push for the win. Since you can also Special Summon The Legendary Insect Queen simply through Contact Fusion, you can retrieve two cards that mention Dark Time Wizard, and quite a few Dark Time Wizard Spells don't have limits on the number of times you can activate them, allowing you to create a massive ATK gap by activating multiple Graceful & Skull Dices to power up your monsters.

Free Agents

Compared to Beyond the Brave, there are significantly more excellent generic cards to be found in Immortal Phoenix.

Heretic Eradicator

When your opponent would Special Summon exactly 1 monster, while this card is in your hand and your opponent has 4 or more monsters that cannot be Normal Summoned/Set in their face-up field, GY, and/or banishment (Quick Effect): You can negate the Summon, and if you do, destroy that monster, and if you do that, Special Summon this card (while you control no monsters, this effect and its activation cannot be negated). You can send this card from the field to the GY; halve the ATK of 1 monster on the field. You can only use each effect of "Heretic Eradicator" once per turn.

Heretic Eradicator is a Special Summon-negation hand trap with the caveat that your opponent has to have put out or milled at least four monsters that can't be Normal Summoned or Set. This might seem steep, but there's a few tweaks that make this effect more flexible than it seems. Firstly, you don't have to negate the Summon of a monster that can't be Normal Summoned or Set, your opponent simply has to have used them. Secondly, this doesn't only apply to Extra Deck monsters, but also to Ritual Monsters and Special Summon monsters like Infernoid and Drytrons. Finally, if you use this while you control no monsters, your opponent can't negate it. 

You can also send Heretic Eradicator to the graveyard to halve the ATK of a monster, which isn't bad, but the real use of this effect is to get it off the field so it doesn't interfere with your main strategy.

The Secret Crane Princess Who Returns A Favor

During your opponent's End Phase: You can place this card from your GY on top of the Deck. During the Main Phase (Quick Effect): You can return this card from the field to the hand, and if you do, each player draws 1 card, then your opponent can draw 1 card, and if they do, you must keep your hand revealed during this Main Phase. (Quick Effect): You can banish this revealed card from your hand; destroy all face-up cards your opponent controls. You can only use each effect of "The Secret Crane Princess Who Returns A Favor" once per turn.

It's obvious looking at The Secret Crane Princess Who Returns A Favor that she's intended to counter the pain in the backside that is Mind Scan and similar hand revealing effects. If she's revealed in your hand, you can destroy all your opponent's face-up cards, and you can force her to be revealed yourself by returning her from the field to the hand, making both players draw, and then allowing your opponent to draw again; it's sort of like the reverse of the Maxx "C" challenge in a way. As a final bonus, she can return herself from the graveyard to the top of your deck, just in case you need to continually have her in your hand to counter your opponent.

Lethargisaurus

1 Defense Position Tuner + 1+ Defense Position non-Tuners

If this card is Special Summoned in Attack Position: Change it to Defense Position. This Defense Position card gains these effects.

  • Change all face-up monsters on the field to Defense Position.
  • Neither player can activate cards or effects in response to the activation of their own cards or effects.
  • Once per turn, during the End Phase: Each player gains 500 LP for each Defense Position monster they control.

Lethargisaurus is going to catch so many duelists out no matter who's using it. Someone will be caught off guard by the fact he requires Defense Position Synchro Materials; someone will forget that he prevents them from chaining multiple effects when they use monsters as material, and someone is definitely going to forget that he can't do much against Link Monsters. 

All that said, Lethargisaurus is a potent stall monster that switches all face-up monsters on the field to Defense Position as long as he's in Defense Position, giving both players an LP boost for those monsters, and blunting a long of modern combos by preventing players from activating cards or effects in response to their own. 

Karin the Celestial Sage of the Highest Heights

2 Level 7 monsters

When your opponent activates a card or effect that includes an effect that Special Summons a monster(s) from the Deck (Quick Effect): You can detach 1 material from this card; your opponent draws 1 card, then negate that activated effect, and if you do, destroy that card. During your Main Phase 2: You can target 1 Level 7 monster in your GY; take damage equal to its ATK, and if you do, return both it and this card on the field to the hand/Extra Deck. You can only use each effect of "Karin the Celestial Sage of the Highest Heights" once per turn.

Karin the Celestial Sage of the Highest Heights is the tie-in card for Raise Moon in Immortal Phoenix, not technically part of the theme, but designed to support it. This Rank 7 Xyz Monster can counter cards or effects that would Special Summon a monster from the deck while also forcing your opponent to draw. She also has a unique second effect that returns her from the field and a Level 7 monster from the graveyard to the hand or Extra Deck, albeit at the cost of taking damage equal to that monster's ATK, allowing you to easily resummon her with fresh materials.

Necromancer of Dragon Magic

2 Effect Monsters

During your Main Phase: You can reveal 1 Fusion Monster in your Extra Deck, choose 1 non-Fusion Monster in your GY whose name is mentioned on the revealed monster, and this card's name becomes that monster's (until the End Phase), then you can Fusion Summon the revealed Fusion Monster, by banishing its materials from your hand, field, and/or GY, also you cannot Special Summon from the Extra Deck for the rest of this turn, except Fusion Monsters. You can only use this effect of "Necromancer of Dragon Magic" once per turn.

I love this card (and I really like Keeper of Dragon Magic back when it came out). Necromancer of Dragon Magic is a boon for Fusion Decks that use Fusion Monsters with named materials, copying the name of that material as long as it's in your graveyard and then Fusion Summoning the appropriate Fusion Monster using materials from your hand, field or graveyard. It can copy the name of a Fusion Material when the Fusion Monster requires a named monster and monsters of the Type or theme and then Fusion Summon it then and there, or you can Fusion Summon without using Necromancer as the material and leverage its new name for other effects. 

Really, any effect that performs a Fusion Summon on another Extra Deck is bound to be brilliant.

Power of the Duelist

Declare 2, 3, or 4 Attributes; apply this effect based on the number declared, also during the End Phase of this turn, you must send all cards you control to the GY, unless you have activated effects of monsters of all declared Attributes in your field and/or GY this turn.

  • 2: Target 1 monster on the field; banish it.
  • 3: Draw 2 cards, then discard 1 card.
  • 4: Negate the effects of 2 face-up cards on the field.

You can only activate 1 "Power of the Duelist" per turn.

Power of the Duelist is a deceptively good card! It has three possible effects, depending on the number of Attributes you declare at activation, and if you don't activate the effects of monsters with all of those Attributes that turn (either from your field or graveyard), you'll have to send all your cards to the graveyard. Naturally, there's two paths from there: you can either make sure you'll declare and activate the necessary Attributes… or you can win the duel that turn.

Declare two Attributes, and you get an effective spot removal, but if you declare three you get a generic autocorrection draw effect. Declare four, and you can negate the effects of two cards on the field without targeting them.

The Pyramid of Kepher

Send 1 Zombie Ritual Monster from your Deck to the GY; place 1 Field Spell from your Deck or GY face-up on your field, also you cannot activate non-Zombie monster effects for the rest of this turn after this card resolves. If your opponent controls an Effect Monster: You can banish this card from your GY, then target 1 Ritual Monster in your GY; add it to your hand. You can only use each effect of "The Pyramid of Kepher" once per turn.

This Spell is intended to tie in with the Zenet theme from Glorious Victors but also works with Vendreads. The Pyramid of Kepher sends a Zombie Ritual Monster to the graveyard and then places a Field Spell from your deck or graveyard onto your field, while also locking you into Zombie monster effects for the rest of the turn. Both Zenet and Vendread can Ritual Summon their Ritual Monsters from the graveyard, so this "cost" is more of a boon, but you can also get that Ritual Monster back into your hand by banishing The Pyramid of Kepher from your graveyard if your opponent controls a monster.

Immortal Phoenix is sure to have an impact on the metagame once it releases between the solid new themes and excellent free agents. Given that it's such an awesome set with a ton of cool cards, there were a bunch that I couldn't mention in this article, so feel free to let me know on my socials if I missed any you like!

Pokémon|collecting|finance

The 10 Most Expensive Pokémon Chase Cards in Delta Reign

Everybody loves Rayquaza.

By Peter Day

|

Published Nov 10, 2026

|

6 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

With Delta Reign, the Pokémon Company International is closing out 2026 by continuing the trends we saw throughout the year.

Like Perfect Order, Chaos Rising, and Pitch Black before it, Delta Reign is a relatively small English Pokémon set based on a single Japanese expansion, with one massive headliner as the set's singular focus. This time, that headliner is Rayquaza, a fan-favorite Pokémon on a level beyond that of Zygarde, Greninja, and Darkrai.

As expected, the Special Illustration Rare (SIR) and Mega Hyper Rare (MHR) versions of the Sky-High Pokémon have soared far above everything else in Delta Reign. That doesn't mean you can write off the rest of the set, however. While the other SIRs don't have anything close to Rayquaza's name recognition, more than a few of the Illustration Rares (IRs) in Delta Reign have ascended to chase status—either because the Pokémon they feature are so iconic, or for Tomokazu Komiya reasons.

Let's take a look at some of the Illustration Rares and Special Illustration Rares that are vying to be Rayquaza's opening act. These are the most valuable Pokémon cards in Delta Reign.

#10 Groudon 111/103 (Illustration Rare)

Rayquaza may be the star of Delta Reign, but the other two members of the weather trio haven't been left out. The Continent Pokémon Groudon appears as an Illustration Rare in the set, and the Sea Basin Pokémon Kyogre cameos as the promo card that comes with Delta Reign Elite Trainer Boxes.

Ryota Murayama's blazing-hot illustration adds a third contender for the title of the best-looking full-art Groudon card ever printed, alongside Nurikabe's IR Groudon from Paradox Rift and nagimiso's Team Magma's Groudon-EX. Both of those cards have topped their respective sets' price guides in the past, so it's not surprising that this Groudon has become one of the big chase cards in Delta Reign.

#9 Mega Golisopod ex 135/103 (Special Illustration Rare)

Debuting in cardboard for the first time in Delta Reign, Mega Golisopod ex has a swanky Special Illustration Rare version by prolific Pokémon artist nagimiso, and an attack that's just as appealing. With Finishing Blow, Mega Golisopod ex can deal 220 damage for a single Energy as long as its victim has any damage counters on it already.

Is that strong enough to see play? We'll have to wait until after Dragapult retires from ruling the format to find out. In the meantime, this card's harsh purple, orange, and green color scheme ensures that it stands out.

#8 Aarune 139/103 (Special Illustration Rare)

With his ability to grab multiple Stadium cards, Aarune works great in decks that want to assemble both halves of a Legendary Stadium like Legendary Pyroduct.

That's nifty, but it's not enough to make every Aarune card valuable, as evidenced by his Ultra Rare and Uncommon versions. I also wouldn't attribute the price difference solely to this card's (admittedly adorable) artwork by Shimaris Yukichi.

As far as this card's price goes, its most significant trait is just its Special Illustration Rare (SIR) rarity, typically the most-sought after rarity in modern Pokémon sets. Pokémon fans love high rarities, and art with actual backgrounds, and SIRs check both of those boxes.

#7 Eevee 114/103 (Illustration Rare)

From Growlithe to Azurill to Sprigatito, Delta Reign has an impressive lineup of Illustration Rares featuring beloved Pokémon. But none of them compare to Eevee, the pre-evolution to everyone's favorite Pokémon. (All eight of them).

Eevee has appeared on countless valuable Pokémon cards over the years, and this Illustration Rare continues the trend. Hideki Ishikawa didn't stray too far from the standard Pokémon style guide with this card, but they showed impressive attention to detail with the dappled sunlight and the stitching on the bag.

Most importantly though, this card shows Eevee in the kind of pose that would earn any pet a devoted social media following. Cute things are cute.

#6 Mega Golurk ex 137/103 (Special Illustration Rare)

Mega Golurk is another Mega-Evolved Pokémon that's getting its TCG debut in Delta Reign after appearing in Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

Goliath's Punch comes with too many restrictions and drawbacks to make it appealing to players. Thankfully, the art is attractive enough on its own. Takeshi Nakamura chose the perfect blend of sunset colors to make Mega Golurk's high-contrast yellow-and-purple color scheme look natural, even dignified.

Golurk might not be the highest-profile Pokémon in the franchise, but everyone knows a gorgeous card when they see one.

#5 Kecleon 117/103 (Illustration Rare)

Who would even think to draw a Kecleon pole-dancing in a kaleidoscopic rain forest? Only Tomokazu Komiya.

Komiya uses colors, poses, and backgrounds that wouldn't even occur to a less creative artist. His idiosyncratic style has earned his work a lot of well-deserved attention over the years, and that attention has translated into hype for cards with his name on them—especially the most outlandish ones. No surprise that his latest Crayola fever dream has found an audience.

#4 Zinnia's Trust 140/103 (Special Illustration Rare)

Zinnia earned the respect of Pokémon fans with her determined pursuit of Rayquaza in order to save the planet in Delta Episode.

As a mysterious woman connected to a fan-favorite Pokémon, Zinnia has been an immensely popular character in the franchise, and many of the cards featuring her have been as valuable as that fact implies. Now Zinnia fans have another card to chase like the fate of the world is at stake.

#3 Raikou ex 136/103 (Mega Hyper Rare)

Rayquaza's not the only Legendary Pokémon with a Special Illustration Rare card in Delta Reign. The Thunder Pokémon Raikou also has an SIR, with a stunning illustration by Oku where Raikou appears to be riding lightning down from the mountains.

For a Legendary Gen II Pokémon, Raikou hasn't appeared in many full-art cards over the years, and arguably none of them look as dynamic as this one. Raikou deserved a glow-up like this.

#2 Mega Rayquaza ex 141/103 (Mega Hyper Rare)

Since the start of the Mega Evolution Series in late 2025, every Pokémon set has had one or two gold-colored Mega Hyper Rare cards as their capstones. These are the rarest cards in their respective sets, and while they're not usually the most valuable (fans don't love the monochromatic artwork), their scarcity alone makes them incredibly valuable.

In Delta Reign, the Pokémon that got the Mega Hyper Rare treatment was none other than Mega Rayquaza ex, the set's mascot and strongest new attacker. Obviously, the gold-tinted version of the Pokémon on all the box art was always going to be one of the biggest chase cards in the set.

Just, not the biggest.

#1 Mega Rayquaza ex 138/103 (Special Illustration Rare)

By far, the most expensive Pokémon card in Delta Reign is Special Illustration Rare Mega Rayquaza ex.

Delta Reign is Rayquaza's set, and no version of Mega Rayquaza ex has collectors more excited than the SIR. That largely comes down to the art. While the Mega Hyper Rare version feels opulent, modern Pokémon collectors tend to prefer cards with actual backgrounds that show characters as living parts of the Pokémon world, not as static mascots. And Kazuki Minami's take on Mega Rayquaza is about as far from static as you can get (though it's plenty electric, har har), showing the Sky-High Pokémon in a moment of dynamic exuberance that jolts the viewer awake.
